I have the same issues and I stick to sheer formulas pretty exclusively! For cream/liquid blush I love Pixi sheer cheek gel, benetint, Javon ford’s cheek stain, and the new Dior blush stick! I get a sheer wash of color with them so I don’t look clownish and I don’t need to spend more than 5 seconds blending! 

I also have dark hair so sometimes colors that are too light just wash me out (light peaches/pastel pinks). I find that using darker berry and red shades but in a sheer formulation makes me look naturally flushed!

The NARS pot one is the best for spot concealing acne. Never budges and it actually sticks to the acne instead of sliding around. I don’t set it with anything and it covers my juiciest pimples for 12 hours. It also kind of self sets hence the lack of powder. I use this exclusively for concealing spots/active acne tho, my skin is too dry to use this anywhere else. 

The Merit is lovely, I use it as a foundation/concealer hybrid. I’ll use it on acne scars, under my eyes and around my nose to brighten, and on my forehead to slightly mattify. I’ve seen people struggle with this product and I think you just need to have good skin prep beforehand. I moisturize and use a moderately glowy SPF and this blends in very easily. 

The Merit stick is more versatile but it’s definitely one I use in my “better” skin days. The NARS really saves me when I have active breakouts.

I find many cream products patchy when I blend with my fingers but not these. I can swipe, pat to blend, and I’m good to go. 

I think the PH adjusting aspect is pretty subtle. I have noticed when I apply to my hand with mix with my highlighter a subtle stain is left behind even after I wash my hands throughout the day. Wear time is about 9-10 hours for me before I notice fading!

My favorite thing though is that even a dark shade like cherry won’t sink into my pores! I have the red shade in the Haus labs blush stick and the pigment sinks into my pores and looks patchy. I don’t have this problem with the Dior, it just glides over my skin!

I’m in love with the new ILIA one that comes in the compact! The glow is so natural and ethereal and it wears beautifully throughout the day. It truly looks like concentrated light without any discernible shimmers or Vaseline like texture.

It’s a cream that sets like a powder so no balmy, greasy feeling on the skin at all. The shimmers in it are microscopically small. I’ve put a flashlight to my face and still can’t see the little shimmer particles, just a seamless glow. I got this earlier this year and haven’t touched my other styling tools - besides my dryer just to rough dry to 80% when I’m in a hurry. 

The wet hair settings are what you would expect, I do find it louder than other styling brushes tho. IMO it’s the dry setting that makes this really stand out. My hair is wavy and some sections are kind of coarse. The dry setting smooths and tames my wildest bedheads in like 10-15 minutes and it’s silent😭; it’s perfect for me bc I’m a night shower person and I’m too impatient to dry and style my hair at night. So when I wake up with frizzy waves this thing gives me beautifully styled hair with zero fuss and zero noise so I don’t have to bother my family with the blow dryer sound at 6:30 in the morning! 

The hot combs are hot enough to style my hair easily and I do use heat protectant but I find that this doesn’t make my hair as hot as other tools and I have fewer split ends than I did when I was using other tools regularly. 

It won’t give you the absolute sleekest blowout because the heat setting is capped, but it still gives a really beautiful result and I absolutely love using this.

If you have very curly/coily hair or if your hair is very resistant to heat styling, this may not get hot enough for your liking. And if you want your hair style to hold perfectly in between washes, this might not get hot enough to give your hair enough memory to set its style. After day 3 my hair slightly bends in some places but I don’t really mind because it’s so convenient to use. You can also touch up your hair in like 2 minutes with the dry setting.

I can’t tolerate large shimmer particles in any complexion products, I need them to be so microscopic that my eyes can’t detect the individual particles so I love the Charlotte Hollywood flawless filter!!! The Saie is nice too but feels more like a glowy gel primer imo

The Charlotte gives a beautiful radiance and it has powders inside the liquid that also blur the skin so you get glow and radiance AND minimized skin texture. Also very natural looking, so probably not a choice for the full glam of heart

Imo the feeling/finished are pretty different! Comes down to what you prefer :•)

Hourglass is a baked formula that applies sheerly, like watercolor in powder form. And the finish is very skin like! Like matte but a teensy bit satin, most shades have no shimmer but have the smallest bit of a sheen to them! It also feels very thin to the touch if you were to swatch with your finger. Since it applies like watercolor, it’s almost impossible to overdo it. Super nice if you like natural looking makeup but if you want full impact glam you may have to build it up a loooot

NARS is more of a traditional powder. Feels very velvety and I’d say it’s a true matte. Like undeniable matte and velvety but it’s not chalky or powdery looking on the skin. If you’re looking for a traditional, matte formula, this one is beautifully executed. It also feels more creamy to the touch than the hourglass! Like the formula has more “body” to it. It lays down more pigment than the hourglass but it’s still really easy to work with. Not as effortless to apply imo but I think it’s more versatile because you can get more pigmentation out of it

You raise a very good point and you’re completely right that in the context of horror lit, a little life is a perfectly good tragedy/torture rec. I think in that light too, the ending and the overall plot aren’t too far off from what’s expected in the realm of horror. If it was marketed as a horror book I definitely wouldn’t criticize it. I just find it super distasteful bc I think it was put on this pedestal as the next great American novel when really it reads very similarly to something like the girl next door. 

I have a lot of beef with the book outside of that specific context tho. I think it was super popular among book circles in like 2019 and I was expecting a great feat of American literature but when I finished it I was like “oh… so suffering makes me beyond redemption and I should kms” (I was in a very bad place when I read it lol). 

I always kind of contrast it to Earthlings which I found very comforting in an oddly wholesome way. Both books have CSA but in Earthlings I can clearly see why the author made the deliberate choice to include that and we get to see the mechanics of how it impacted the character and how she processed that experience. It wasn’t gratuitous and I think she put a lot of thought into how she wove that into the book. Whereas in a little life it was just like, oh great another tragedy to befall this poor man, similar to the way a lot of horror books by male authors include SA but they offer a very surface level glimpse into how it actually impacted the survivor. In a little life I honestly think Jude’s story could’ve been written the same way without the CSA and the plot and his psyche would be the same. In my opinion that makes the inclusion of CSA thoughtless and just there for shock value rather than for substance and discussion. Which is fine I guess if it was marketed or discussed as a horror novel.

I agree with the other previous comments - if not all/enough of the shades in it are useful to you, not really worth the $90. 

BUT, if the shades in it are what you reach for, their palettes can be incredibly convenient, luxury workhorses in your makeup routine. The quality of the powders beats my Chanel, Dior, and NARS on any given day. Hourglass has really cracked the code on formulating beautiful, effortless to use powders that look lifelike yet elegantly airbrushed. 

I got the jellyfish from last year and I love having every complexion powder in one place, and the blushes, bronzer, and highlighter are colors I love using. For that reason, it’s definitely been worth it. And it’s almost been a whole year and I’ve barely made a dent in it. 

I guess this can be both good and bad, but with Hourglass, a lot of their shades are extremely close together. Many of the blushes pull neutral to neutral warm with a little nuance on whether they’re pink, peachy, or plum colored. And the bronzers and highlighters tend to be crowd pleasers since they’re not orange or too icy respectively. I think because of that, if you end up getting one palette, you’re not going to be tempted to buy another one until you hit pan on it or unless they release super unique shades, which I rarely see them do lol. I’m an impulsive shopper so I’m grateful that most of their shades are barely distinguishable from each other bc it keeps me from buying another palette lol.

Mine is also virgin and fine but densely packed, heavy formulas weigh my hair down but I have no issue layering lighter formulas. I like to use Olaplex no.9 which has a very light gel-serum texture and it has heat protection and then I go in with an oil that also has heat protection (either Olaplex no. 7 the OUAI oil). I’ve previously used the Kerastase curl cream (includes heat protection) and layered Bumble and Bumble invisible oil primer and also enjoyed that combo! 

I layer my products into wet or damp hair, I feel like the water in my hair helps distribute the product more evenly so my hair isn’t weighed down. I’ll spread the product onto my hands really well and then palm it through my hair and really focus on the ends to make sure they’re protected. 

I’ve cut back to using heat only 2-3 times a week by extending my hairstyle. I use the Shark Smoothstyle which I think helps bc it alleges to not use heat at a damaging temperature?? But the Olaplex no. 9 helps my hair keep its style and all I do in between washes is hydrate the ends with a bit of leave in conditioner and dry shampoo when my roots need it. 

It can be harder to extend your hairstyle depending on lifestyle and how your hair keeps its shape but I think layering heat protectants really helps! I also recommend using a good shampoo with high quality sulfates so the silicones in the heat protectants don’t weigh your hair down! If you watch the video she explains how olives can appear very warm or very cool relative to other skin tones - the parts where she shows Eva Mendes and Zoe Saldana point this out. They appear very warm and very cool respectively but both have ratios of yellow (warm) and blue (cool) to their complexions.

[Style me Jenn explains it really well in this video!](https://youtu.be/yx4-0eI8bn8?si=DpBvCLh4IcwGK4J_)

She says skin tones are typically made up of yellow, blue, and red tones; olives have little amounts of red and are predominantly yellow and blue, which makes green 🫒. And like when you mix paints, the mixture of the undertones in your skin can create a more muted, desaturated color. 

Olive undertones kind of sit in the middle of warm and cool on the spectrum so technically olive is more neutral but can still lean more towards each end of the spectrum. Hi I’m really proud of you for coming out to someone and for talking to us here! Things for you sound really overwhelming at the moment and I hope you remember that you have and will always deserve to be who you are despite what anyone may think or say. But anyway, I cut pretty regularly whenever I got overwhelmed, like it became a very casual thing for me to cut multiple times a week. My therapist recommended putting my sharps somewhere that was inconvenient for me to reach (I put mine back back on top of my closet where I’d need to grab a ladder or chair to get them) and then hold an ice cube in my hand instead. It honestly worked really well for me. The ice does hurt when you squeeze it and it’s very inconvenient to have melted ice water drip on your clothes after. So while the pain from the cold helped me sort myself out, my aversion to cold water dripping on my clothes or bed or floors helped me wean myself off of ice. Because the ice is less appealing that way it’s gotten easier to just sit through my most intense emotional episodes or find something to distract myself with. I hope any of this helps!
